versions.short: The law requires federal officials to jointly develop a standard chemical-analysis method for identifying where seafood comes from, to help enforce against illegal, unreported, or unregulated fishing and seafood fraud. The method must be usable by law enforcement, quick to process, and testable with a field kit one person can carry, and it must also work, where practical, on prepared seafood dishes such as sushi and ceviche. Officials must run pilot studies on red snapper and tuna, and within two years report to Congress on the method, a plan to put it into use, and whether any part of it is impractical.
